Jack's Daily News

No. 4· 3 September 2026· Global, Italy in focus· Illustrated edition
In three lines

  1. Nostalgia turns from an aesthetic into the default growth lever this week: Pinterest's new Hobbies trend report shows searches for "herbal apothecary" up 595% and "candle making tutorial" up 118% (Pinterest Newsroom, 2 Sep 2026), while a revived 2009 home video drives a new TikTok audio trend.

  2. Digiday reports the first real cracks in creator economy pricing: Emma Chamberlain calls it a bubble "bursting in slow motion," and talent agency Sway says brands overpay creators 90% of the time (Digiday, 2 Sep 2026).

The world

9to5Google · 4 Aug 2026, effective 4 Sep 2026

Google retires Assistant for Gemini, starting tomorrow

Google begins pulling Google Assistant from Android phones, tablets, Wear OS watches and Android Auto starting September 4. Gemini takes over as the default assistant, the rollout reaches all users within a few weeks, and there is no way to switch back. Assistant survives for now only in cars with "Google built-in" and keeps running on Google TV, Home speakers and smart displays, where Gemini arrives on its own separate timeline.

Why it mattersThe assistant most brands built a decade of voice search and skills around disappears in weeks, not years. Any voice or smart-speaker strategy tuned for Assistant needs a Gemini-native rewrite, with no transition window to test it in.
Digiday · 2 Sep 2026

The creator economy shows its first real cracks

A survey of 1,000 marketing and procurement leaders, run for talent agency Sway, finds brands misprice creator fees roughly half the time and feel they overpaid on 40% of deals. Sway's CEO Danielle Wiley puts the real overpay rate at 90%. Creator Emma Chamberlain says the bubble is "bursting in slow motion." At the same time, influencer marketing agencies are automating deal-making the way programmatic advertising automated media buying, which strips individual creators of negotiating leverage as creator supply keeps growing faster than advertiser demand. Digiday sizes the market at $43.9 billion for 2026.

Why it mattersThis is the same season Meta says Partnership Ads hit a $10 billion run rate because creator content beats brand content (issue no. 3). Both are true at once: creator content is winning the format war and losing the pricing war, because supply grew faster than anyone's ability to value it.
Digiday · 6 Aug 2026

OpenAI brings product carousels to ChatGPT ads

OpenAI now lets several products from one retailer appear together in a carousel at the bottom of a ChatGPT conversation, instead of showing one product at a time. The company is targeting $2.5 billion in ad revenue for 2026 and, per its own investor materials, over $100 billion by 2030, a 40x jump. An unnamed agency executive told Digiday the timing is about the fourth quarter: "the holiday shopping season is coming, so OpenAI wants to make sure that these products are discoverable in ChatGPT conversations."

Why it mattersA chat interface is becoming a shelf. The carousel is the same unit Google Shopping and Amazon trained everyone to scan, now sitting inside a conversation with no visible competitor set. Whoever fixes their product feed before Q4 gets first-mover pricing on attention that is not yet being auctioned.
Retail Dive, Fashionista · Sep 2026

Sephora launches a recurring drop shop on TikTok Shop

Sephora's Drop Shop goes live September 19 on TikTok Shop, with exclusive monthly product launches, creator content and celebrity-hosted TikTok Lives that reveal what is available right after the stream. It lands as TikTok Shop closes H1 2026 at $50.3 billion in global sales, up 92% year over year, with $11.8 billion of that in the US alone.

Why it mattersSephora is not testing TikTok Shop, it is building a recurring release calendar around it, the same mechanic drop culture uses in sneakers and streetwear. On a channel growing 92% a year, arriving late now costs more than it did twelve months ago.

Social trends

Pinterest Newsroom · 2 Sep 2026

Pinterest's "Kitchen Witch" wave

  • Pinterest's "Find Your Joy" 2026 Hobbies Trend Report ties its "Kitchen Witch" trend to a Warner Bros partnership for Practical Magic 2.
  • Searches: "herbal apothecary" up 595%, "midnight margaritas" up 140%, "candle making tutorial" up 118% (Pinterest Newsroom).
  • Status: hot, tied to a specific film release so likely to compress fast once the cycle passes.
Why it mattersA search platform is now timing a lifestyle trend to a movie release date, which means the trend has a built-in expiry that brands riding it should plan around.
NapoleonCat, SocialPilot, Ramdam · late Aug/early Sep 2026

TikTok's "My American Girl Doll" audio

  • A 2009 home video of a kid introducing his doll "Mia" with full enthusiasm is now the backing audio for creators revealing the grown-up version of a prized possession.
  • Status: rising. No verified view count found for the audio itself, flagged here.
Why it mattersBoth this trend and Pinterest's Kitchen Witch wave monetize the same emotion through opposite channels, search intent on one platform, audio revival on the other. Nostalgia is not one trend right now, it is the operating system several trends are running on.

Campaigns & brand moves

Retail Gazette, FashionUnited · Aug 2026

Burberry, "Heads back to the city"

Burberry's Autumn 2026 campaign turns the London commute itself into the subject. Models Rosemary Ferguson, Cherif Douamba and Haojie Qi navigate rush hour at Blackfriars Bridge and a tube station entrance, narrated by Matthew Streeton, one of the real voices behind London transport announcements. The collection (Foxfield and Mayfair trenches, cashmere knitwear) is styled as transitional dressing, not statement pieces.

Why it mattersThe mechanism is borrowed authority. Streeton's voice does not describe the coat, it makes the commute itself feel narrated, and the ad rides on a sound Londoners already trust from daily life.
ADC Group, Brand News · rebrand 18 Jun 2026, spot on air 6 Jul-Sep 2026

Calvé, "Un classico italiano"

Calvé (Unilever) refreshed its visual identity, logo, packaging and photography, keeping its signature yellow while softening the letterforms around "creaminess," and moved from condiment-style product shots to macro close-ups of ingredients inside classic Italian recipes. The new spot, by AUGE Communication with Think Cattleya and Mindshare, runs on a 60% TV, 40% digital split. Communication investment for 2026 is triple 2025's, per the brand.

Why it mattersThe repositioning is not cosmetic, it moves the product from garnish to ingredient inside the shot itself, which is the actual claim the tripled budget is paying to prove.

What is working in content

Social Media Today, Mumbrella, BestMediaInfo · 2 Sep 2026

Reddit's 15-second Engaged Video Views

Reddit's new billing option counts a video view only once someone watches at least 15 seconds, or the whole clip if it runs shorter. In alpha testing this pushed 15-second view-through rate up 51% and completion rate up 71% versus the old metric; The Times ran a split test and confirmed gains in view rate, completion, click-through rate and cost.

Why it mattersPlatforms keep moving the unit they sell from "seen" to "watched," first YouTube's satisfaction signals (issue no. 3), now Reddit's 15-second floor. A format built for the old vanity metric, the fast tease, gets punished under the new one, which rewards a video that earns its first 15 seconds honestly.
Pinterest Newsroom · 2 Sep 2026

Pinterest's tutorial format, inside the nostalgia wave

Inside the same Hobbies report, the search that is up 118% is specifically "candle making tutorial," not "candles." The format doing the work is the instructional how-to, not the finished product shot.

Why it mattersNostalgia sells better as a skill you can learn than as a mood you can look at. The actionable format converts intent into a saved search, which is Pinterest's real currency.

The historical bridge

1975, Parma

Mulino Bianco invents a past for a product born in 1975

Barilla launches Mulino Bianco, a new bakery brand, and bets the entire positioning on memory instead of product claims. The first ad airs on Carosello in 1976: "Filastrocche," nursery rhymes told by a mother to her child, no biscuit in sight. Through the Eighties the country mill run by the "Piccolo Mugnaio Bianco" becomes a fixed, recognizable place; in 1990 agency Armando Testa reframes it as the destination of a family exhausted by city life, fleeing to a water mill. Mulino Bianco turned 50 in 2025 with a campaign that deliberately reused the same symbols, testing which memories from the archive still land with people who never saw the originals.

Why it still holds. Barilla did not sell nostalgia for something old, it invented a past for a product launched in 1975 and sold that instead. That is the same move behind this week's "Kitchen Witch" search spike and the "My American Girl Doll" audio trend, both selling a past that only part of the audience actually lived through. Fifty years on, the lesson holds: nostalgia marketing does not require the audience to remember the thing, it requires the brand to build the memory convincingly enough that people adopt it as their own.
